rationale:
D17/D27/D18, the `returnType` half of the decorated head. A macro standing where a return type stands is a DECORATOR, and this lane published the macro spelling as the C++ return type: measured over the 465-file cpp corpus, 121 symbols named a macro there (42 DOCTEST_INTERFACE, 36 JSON_HEDLEY_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT, 12 DOCTEST_APPROX_PREFIX, 8 JSON_HEDLEY_NON_NULL, 8 JSON_HEDLEY_DEPRECATED_FOR, …, 14 distinct spellings), and a macro name is not a type any compiler accepts — it resolves to nothing, in a field the store treats as an overload-resolution input. The same nodes produced a second defect, worse because both endpoints resolve: `JSON_HEDLEY_NON_NULL(3) invalid_iterator(int id_, const char* what_arg) : exception(id_, what_arg) {}` published `method invalid_iterator.exception` — a member named after the class's own BASE, with NO parameters and a body it does not have, while the constructor itself was never published (4 sites on this corpus: invalid_iterator/type_error/out_of_range/other_error in nlohmann/detail/exceptions.hpp). The pre-fix reader took the direct child of the recovery's `parenthesized_declarator`, which on that shape is the base-class initializer read as a declarator, and the real one sits one level deeper inside the grammar's own ERROR.

The pins are the five measured head shapes, each with the evidence it turns on: a `macro_prefixed_type_specifier` (the grammar's own decorator/type split), a type whose alignment padding must not survive into the field (D27), a type left inside the recovery's ERROR, a type REJOINED to the name as a phantom qualifier (empty `::`), and a constructor's decorated head — which states NO type, so `returnType` is pinned as `null` (the ABSENT assertion this matcher supports). Three controls keep the rule honest from the other side: `HANDLE_CTX` is an all-caps TYPEDEF (the spelling alone can never be the test — the marker rule's own measurement over the two pinned corpora found 43 such false positives and lists HANDLE/DWORD/WORD among them), a decorated declaration still earns its own symbol, and a macro INVOCATION recovered into a declaration-shaped node (the preprocessor-split body at nlohmann json.hpp:3499) must not be published as the function its CALL's declarator names — the recovery may only be entered for a declaration that states a type or defines something.

expectReturnType.note: the specifier's non-macro children. Pre-fix this read `LIB_API void`: one function, two return types in one index, because its out-of-line definition in a .cpp states `void`.

D27, and the only row that fails if the whitespace normalisation is dropped: the source writes the type with alignment padding, and `unsigned   long   long` is not a spelling of any C++ type a compiler accepts.

the recovery's ERROR holds TWO decorators, the type and the declarator — measured on nlohmann to_chars.hpp:1063, where the pre-fix reader published NOTHING at all (the declarator is inside the ERROR, one level below the wrapper's direct children), so this row is also a coverage gain. The pointer is dropped, which is this analyzer's existing convention for every pointer return type (`char* f()` publishes `char`).

the type the grammar rejoined to the NAME. Measured on doctest.h:665 (`DOCTEST_INTERFACE String operator+`), where the qid's separator slot carries an EMPTY `::` — the same evidence `qualifiedDeclaratorLeaf` reads to split name from owner, which is why the two readers cannot disagree.
CONTROL: no decorator, so the declared type is published verbatim.
CONTROL: an all-caps TYPEDEF keeps its field. A rule spelled 'an all-caps spelling in type position is a decorator' would strip this one, and the spelling alone cannot tell it from the marker.

expectSymbols.name: constructor
expectSymbols.note: THE ROW THE MIS-READER COST, twice over. Pre-fix there was no `Sink` constructor at all; instead a `method Sink.Base` — the base-class initializer read as a declarator — carried the body. The parameters are pinned because the declarator that names the function is the same one the signature comes from: the member arm looked it up with a one-level scan that CANNOT see a declarator inside the macro's parens, so the pre-fix symbol had no parameters either. `returnType: null` is the ABSENT assertion: a constructor states no type, and the macro spelling published there was a claim about a signature that does not exist.

expectSymbols.name: first_char
expectSymbols.note: the coverage gain's other half: the pre-fix reader published no symbol here, so these parameters had no home.

expectSymbols.name: Shutdown
expectSymbols.note: CONTROL: the decorator gates the FIELD, never the symbol — a decorated declaration is still a declaration.

expectSymbols.name: getHairColor
expectSymbols.note: CONTROL: the REAL member, declared in `struct Probe`, is published and still owns the name — the gate refuses the recovery, not the name.

forbidSymbols.name: Base
forbidSymbols.note: PRE-FIX, and the reason this fixture exists: the base-class initializer `Base(id, what)` read as a declarator published a member named after the class's own base. Both endpoints of its `contains` edge resolve, so no endpoint-shape audit could see it.

forbidSymbols.name: convert
forbidSymbols.note: PRE-GATE, and the pin that FAILS when the gate is opened: on the preprocessor-split body the recovery's ERROR holds an EXPRESSION (`ptr.convert()`), and a descent that enters every recovery publishes a member named after the CALL — measured on nlohmann json.hpp:3499, where an ungated descent published `function convert`, a name whose only occurrence in the source is a member call inside a return statement. KIND IS DELIBERATELY UNPINNED: the same defect lands as `method` here and as `function` there, so a kind-constrained row would assert nothing on one of the two. Mutating only `enterRecovery` back to `true` makes this row fail while every control still passes.

forbidSymbols.name: LIB_API
forbidSymbols.note: the decorator is never the function: a symbol keyed on the macro would say LIB_API is declared where `void Shutdown()` is written.

forbidSymbols.name: LIB_NONNULL
forbidSymbols.note: same, on the shape where the macro's own argument list is what parses as a declarator (the reader that took the wrapper's direct child was one node away from publishing this).

forbidRelationships.note: the containment edge that the pre-fix symbol owned: `Sink` contains its base-class CALL read as a member. A class does not contain its base's initializer, and `extends Sink -> Base` is the edge that does describe the relationship.

expectRelationships.note: CONTROL, and the row that says the fix did not cost the real relationship: `class Sink : public Base` still extends.
